summary.en: Gunmen continue to launch lethal attacks in northern Nigeria, killing civilians in Plateau, shooting Islamic cleric Yahaya Masussuka dead in Katsina, and killing at least 62 people in Binnari, Taraba, prompting mass displacement. Bandits also targeted APC supporters ahead of a rally in Katsina and abducted six residents from the Millennium City estate in Kaduna, while troops foiled a terrorist attack in Sokoto and rescued two abducted herders in Zamfara. Police in Benue arrested 34 suspected foreign nationals and rescued 29 kidnapping victims, and the Niger State Assembly praised the army for stopping a bandit raid. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn fortsetter å utføre dødelige angrep i Nord-Nigeria, dreper sivile i Plateau, skyter den islamske lærde Yahaya Masussuka død i Katsina, og dreper minst 62 personer i Binnari, Taraba, noe som fører til massefordrivelse. Banditter målrettet også APC-tilhengere før et møte i Katsina og bortførte seks innbyggere fra Millennium City-området i Kaduna, mens soldater avverget et terrorangrep i Sokoto og reddet to bortførte hyrder i Zamfara. Politiet i Benue arresterte 34 mistenkte utenlandske statsborgere og reddet 29 kidnappingsofre, og Niger-statenes forsamling roste hæren for å ha stoppet et bandittangrep. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
